issue.title: chezmoi gcal config comment pins writer to kellys-macbook-pro, which no host label matches; the Mac's label also drifts

task_type_fields.impact: Following the config comment to make the Mac the single gcal writer (as decision bob-gcal-is-read-only-and-proposes-once requires) would block every sync. Even with the right label, the drifting macOS hostname would make Obsidian's sync on note creation fail with exit 2, visible only in the developer console, on about half the days.
task_type_fields.location: chezmoi home/dot_config/bob/config.yml (commented gcal: block, writer key)
task_type_fields.repro:
The chezmoi-managed `~/.config/bob/config.yml` (source `home/dot_config/bob/config.yml`, added in chezmoi 13744456) ships a commented `gcal:` block with `writer: kellys-macbook-pro`. That is the Mac's Tailscale name, not a label bob computes. bob takes the host label from `$HOSTNAME`, else `hostname`, slugged (`vault_sync::hostname_slug`, src/native/vault_sync.rs:2051).

On the Mac (2026-10-31): `hostname` → `Kellys-MacBook-Pro.local`, so `bob gcal doctor` reports `writer kellys-macbook-pro-local`. Uncommenting the block as written makes `bob gcal sync` exit 2 on every host (`this host is kellys-macbook-pro-local; gcal.writer is kellys-macbook-pro`, src/native/gcal/sync.rs:106-114).

Second part: `scutil --get HostName` is `not set` on the Mac, so macOS derives the kernel hostname from the network. Vault-sync commit subjects alternate almost daily between `vault(kellys-mbp)` and `vault(kellys-macbook-pro-local)` (10-28 06:17→12:30 kellys-mbp, 10-28 13:37→10-29 20:29 -local, 10-29 20:41→10-30 14:30 kellys-mbp, 10-30 15:09→10-31 10:46 -local). Neither the vault-sync LaunchAgent nor the shell profiles set HOSTNAME. Any `gcal.writer` pin therefore fails on alternate days until the Mac's HostName is fixed (`sudo scutil --set HostName Kellys-MacBook-Pro.local`).

Fix: change the comment to `writer: kellys-macbook-pro-local` and add a note that the Mac's HostName must be set first (or that `bob gcal doctor` prints the label to use). Optionally document the HostName requirement in bob-cli docs/gcal.md § Where it runs. Full research: research:202610/mac_bob_gcal_sync_setup.md.

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching how to make bob gcal sync work on the Mac: the commented writer value would block sync everywhere, and the Mac's unset HostName makes any writer pin flaky.

evidence.note: Independent repro 2026-11-07 during gmail sync research: ssh mac shows scutil --get HostName still 'not set', hostname=Kellys-MacBook-Pro.local; vault commits keep alternating (kellys-mbp on 11-02/11-04/11-06, kellys-macbook-pro-local on 11-06/11-07); ~/bob/.bob/gmail/ now has two host journals (kellys-macbook-pro-local.jsonl, kellys-mbp.jsonl). New impact: gmail.writer pins break the same way, blocking the planned 15-minute bob gmail sync cron job on the Mac; three gmail research reports proposed writer: kellys-macbook-pro, which matches neither slug. The chezmoi cron machines map (mac: [Kellys-MacBook-Pro]) may also miss the Mac on kellys-mbp days (unverified).

payload.description: Check whether the existing Mac hostname drift bead matches my gmail sync finding

evidence.note: Independent repro 2026-11-07 ~17:15 EST while verifying cronctl (tale for epic bob-cli-ib): ssh mac shows hostname=Kellys-MBP, hostname -s=Kellys-MBP, chezmoi execute-template '{{ .chezmoi.hostname }}'=Kellys-MBP, scutil LocalHostName=Kellys-MacBook-Pro, HostName still not set. New impact: the cron: data enrolls the Mac only as mac: [Kellys-MacBook-Pro] (chezmoi truncates Kellys-MacBook-Pro.local at the dot, so it matches only on the -local days). On Kellys-MBP days, cronctl status --all reports mac identity_mismatch ('the host answering for mac (Kellys-MBP) is not enrolled in its own cron: data'), and the cron-machine partial resolves nothing, so the run_onchange crontab hook renders empty and a local chezmoi update -a leaves the Mac crontab unmanaged. That silently defeats bob-cli-if's local-apply step. Fixing the HostName (sudo scutil --set HostName Kellys-MacBook-Pro.local) or enrolling both names in cron.machines.mac (the partial already accepts a list) would converge it.

payload.description: The Mac's drifting hostname (Kellys-MBP vs enrolled Kellys-MacBook-Pro) makes the crontab hook render empty, so the local apply in step 1 silently skips the Mac until bob-cli-ew is fixed or both names are enrolled
